title: Test User Flows
bottom_line: Run this command and Claude writes one browser test per flow in user-flows.md, then keeps the tests in sync as the flows change.

sections.heading: Type the command, with an optional mode and area

blocks.title: The two optional extras
rows: Chooses whether the tests run against your own dev server or a real deployment. You can also say it in words, such as "test against the deployed app" or "test against my dev server".
Free text. Only the flows and tests under that area heading are handled, and the report says so.

cards.title: A user-flows.md
cards.text: Made by `/user-flows:extract-user-flows`. If it is missing, the skill stops and tells you to run that first. The list is the contract; it never invents flows from the code.

cards.title: uv and Python 3
cards.text: The tests are Python and run through `uv`. On first run it adds `pytest-playwright` as a dev dependency and installs the Playwright browser.

cards.title: make
cards.text: Used for the generated `make test-user-flows` target.

cards.title: A running app
cards.text: The app must be startable locally, or reachable at a deployed URL.

blocks.text: Use it when you want to generate, write, sync or update tests for your user flows, for example after `user-flows.md` changes ("sync the flow tests", "cover the new flows"), or to run flow tests against a deployed, staging or production environment.

sections.heading: Each flow in the list becomes one end-to-end test

blocks.title: How each part of a flow is used
rows: Assertions, the checks the test makes
Where to look when a button name or route is unclear

blocks.text: The tests are end-to-end (E2E) tests: they drive the app in a real browser. The goal is one test per flow, no test without a flow and no flow left uncovered without notice. Tests check exactly what the flow's Expected line says can be observed.

blocks.title: What a test looks like
blocks.caption: Each test is named after its flow ID and name, with the exact flow title inside, so a failure traces straight back to the list.

blocks.title: Good to know
items: Tests are grouped into one file per area, `test_<area_slug>.py`, with one test function per flow.
The `# user-flow: UF-NNN hash: ...` line above each test is a sync marker. The hash is the start of a sha256 fingerprint of the flow's entry. Do not edit it by hand; run the skill again to resync.

If a test's starting state cannot be set up (it needs production data, a paid account, a third-party callback, or in remote mode database state with no way to reach it), the test is still written but marked `@pytest.mark.skip(reason="...")` with a one-line reason. A visible gap is better than a fake pass.

sections.heading: Local mode may touch the database, remote mode may not

rows: A dev server the suite starts, or one already running
A real deployment of the app
Playwright, plus Redis and Postgres directly (fixtures, seed scripts, database-level checks), for example to seed a starting row or check a record was saved
Only Playwright (the browser) and plain HTTP calls to the app's own endpoints, such as its API or the webhooks it exposes
Direct Redis and Postgres access is allowed
A direct database or cache connection, even if credentials happen to be available
Started by the tests when it is not already responding, and stopped after
Never started or stopped; the URL is assumed to be serving already

blocks.title: How the mode is chosen

nodes.label: Look at the configured base URL

blocks.caption: The base URL comes from `conftest.py` or `pyproject.toml`. Unclear means a first run with no clues. A localhost or 127.0.0.1 URL, or no config yet, means local.

blocks.text: The same test files serve both modes. The report says which mode was used and how it was chosen.

sections.heading: The first run sets up Playwright for you

steps.title: Install the test tools
steps.text: If `pytest-playwright` is not among the project's dependencies, it runs these. If the project is not a uv project yet, it runs `uv init` first.

block.code:
uv add --dev pytest-playwright
uv run playwright install chromium

steps.title: Record the app's address
steps.text: The base URL goes into `pyproject.toml` as `--base-url=<app url>` in `addopts` under `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`. In local mode it works out the dev server's URL and start command from the repo. In remote mode it uses the deployment's real URL and asks you for it if it is not in the repo's config or environment.

steps.title: Arrange starting the app
steps.text: Local mode: a fixture in `conftest.py` starts the app when it is not responding and stops it after. If the start command cannot be worked out, the report says the app must be running before the tests. Remote mode: nothing is started.

blocks.text: If Python Playwright is already set up, it uses the existing config, browsers and conventions instead of adding a second setup.

sections.heading: Every run makes sure three project pieces exist

cards.title: Left out by default
cards.text: A `user_flow` marker in `pyproject.toml`, plus `-m "not user_flow"` in `addopts`, keeps these slow browser tests out of a plain `pytest` run. Adding `-m user_flow` includes them.

cards.title: A make target
cards.text: A `test-user-flows` target in the project's `Makefile`, which is created if there is none.

cards.title: A CLAUDE.md note
cards.text: A short section on where the tests live, how they are made, why they are left out by default and how to run them.

blocks.caption: Only missing pieces are added. If the project already leaves tests out another way, that way is kept.

blocks.title: The make target
blocks.code:
.PHONY: test-user-flows
test-user-flows:
	uv run pytest -m user_flow <tests-dir>

blocks.title: What the CLAUDE.md note says
blocks.text: User-flow tests live in the tests folder, are made from `user-flows.md` by `/user-flows:test-user-flow`, are left out of the default pytest run by the `user_flow` marker, and run with `make test-user-flows`. The `# user-flow: UF-NNN hash: ...` comments are sync markers that must not be edited by hand.

sections.heading: Running it again only changes tests whose flow changed

rows: The existing test is edited in place, keeping manual improvements that do not contradict the new flow.
The test is deleted. An area file is deleted only when no tests remain in it.
The test is left exactly as it was.

cards.title: Suspicious deletion
cards.text: If a removed flow's feature clearly still exists in the code, the test is flagged instead of deleted.

points.text: The likely fault is an outdated user-flows.md: run `/user-flows:update-user-flows`.

blocks.title: Where the tests live
items: An existing folder that already holds `user-flow:` markers.
Otherwise, the project's Playwright test folder.

sections.heading: It checks its own work before reporting

steps.title: Every flow in sync
steps.text: Every flow must now show as in sync with its test.

steps.title: Every test file loads
steps.text: This catches syntax and loading errors in every test file.

steps.title: New and changed tests run
steps.text: If the app cannot be started here, it says so. A test that fails because the app really does not do what the flow says is reported as a finding, not bent until it passes.

steps.title: Normal test run unaffected
steps.text: A plain collect still leaves out the user-flow tests and collects the rest of the suite.

sections.heading: Run the tests any time with make test-user-flows

blocks.title: What the report tells you

cards.title: Mode
cards.text: Local or remote, and how it was chosen.

cards.title: Tests by outcome
cards.text: Created (IDs), updated (IDs and what changed), deleted (IDs and files), skipped (IDs and reason), and the unchanged count.

cards.title: Other files touched
cards.text: Project files changed outside the tests folder: `pyproject.toml`, `Makefile`, `CLAUDE.md`.

cards.title: Check results
cards.text: Whether the tests loaded, ran, or could not run, and why.

blocks.caption: It reminds you that the suite runs with `make test-user-flows`, and does not paste whole test files into the conversation.

sections.heading: The defaults and how to change them

rows: Tests are Python Playwright (`pytest-playwright`) run through `uv`
An existing folder with `user-flow:` markers, or the project's Playwright test folder, is used instead
Tests are marked `user_flow` and left out of the normal `pytest` run
Local mode (tests may seed Redis or Postgres directly) when the base URL is localhost; remote mode (UI and HTTP only) for a deployed URL

blocks.text: There are no environment variables and no plugin settings. The base URL the tests use is written to `pyproject.toml`.

next_action.text: With a `user-flows.md` in your project, run `/user-flows:test-user-flow`.
next_action.detail: If there is no user-flows.md yet, run `/user-flows:extract-user-flows` first.
